kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: Generic (no manufacturer branding printed on the ELEGOO-supplied board); the receiver IC's datasheet is published under the VS1838B part designation
identity.manufacturer_part_number: VS1838B (best match to the fetched datasheet; ELEGOO's own product pages could not be loaded to confirm the exact silkscreen on the physical part)
identity.package: module (3-pin through-hole IR receiver in a small black epoxy dome, either bare or soldered to a tiny breakout PCB)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small sensor that listens for the invisible blinking light from an infrared remote control and turns it into an electrical signal the Arduino can read.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Letting the Arduino receive button presses from the kit's included infrared remote control, for example to control an LED, a motor, or an on-screen menu.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Inside the black dome is a photodiode tuned to see only light that blinks 38,000 times per second (38 kHz), the flicker rate used by most IR remotes. A small chip inside filters out sunlight and lamp flicker, then outputs a clean digital pulse train that matches the remote's code.

pinout.name: OUT
pinout.notes: Goes low briefly when it detects an IR pulse; connect to an Arduino digital input pin

pinout.name: VCC
pinout.notes: Connect to Arduino 5V (module accepts 2.7-5.5V per datasheet)

pins.pin_1_identification: Looking at the flat back face of the black dome with the three legs pointing toward you, the legs read left to right as OUT, GND, VCC. This order is confirmed in the fetched VS1838B datasheet's own labeled pinout diagram.

electrical.max_current: 1.5 mA (no-signal quiescent maximum per datasheet; current rises briefly while decoding a signal)
electrical.logic_level: Output swings between about 0.2-0.4V (logic low) and 4.5V+ (logic high) at a 5V supply; compatible with 5V Arduino digital inputs

key_specs.reception_distance: about 18-20 m to a standard remote, per datasheet test conditions

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A small black plastic dome (like a squashed bead), roughly 6-7mm across and 5mm deep, mounted on three thin metal legs about 2.5cm long; sometimes sold pre-soldered to a small breakout PCB with a 3-pin header instead.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Black or dark epoxy dome; tiny white text such as 'VS1838B', 'HX1838', or just '1838' is sometimes printed on the flat back face or on the breakout PCB silkscreen.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: VS1838B, HX1838, TL1838, or '1838' on the dome's flat face or on the small PCB it may be mounted to.
easily_confused_with: A standard 5mm IR LED (the remote's own transmitter, which is clear or bluish, not black)
a generic phototransistor or photodiode used for visible-light sensing

example_connections.uno_pin: D11 (illustrative; any free digital pin works)

required_extra_parts: the kit's IR remote control (needs a CR2025 coin cell, not included)

hazards: Ordinary static sensitivity like any small semiconductor
handling_notes: Bend the legs gently only near the base, never right at the plastic body
Double check VCC/GND orientation before powering up; reversing them can kill the internal IC
common_mistakes: Operating it near fluorescent or some LED lighting, which can flood it with interference
Expecting it to work through walls or at angles beyond about 45 degrees off-axis

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: No response at all from the remote
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Reversed VCC/GND, dead coin cell in the remote, or wrong pin number in the sketch
symptoms_and_causes.check: Confirm 5V at VCC with a multimeter, replace the remote's battery, verify the OUT pin matches the pin defined in code

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Weak remote battery or a damaged receiver
symptoms_and_causes.check: Swap the remote's battery; view the remote's LED through a phone camera, which can often see it blink

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Nearby fluorescent lighting or another IR source interfering
symptoms_and_causes.check: Move away from lights and direct sunlight, then retest

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the module powered, measure DC voltage between VCC and GND to confirm 5V is present. Then measure OUT to GND: it should sit high (near VCC) with no IR present and dip low briefly when a remote button is pressed and pointed at it.
